name: MiMo-V2.6-Pro-MOPD

lineage.how_derived: multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD2, technical report section 5.6) on top of the RL checkpoint, plus a short specialized-teacher run against tool-call repetition

purpose: The builder presents it as the MOPD upgrade of MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL: it fuses domain-specialized teachers into one model, extends to domains where training-time verification is hard (long-horizon game development, scientific research, embodied intelligence) and mitigates tool-call repetition, a failure mode in which the model keeps issuing the same tool calls.

license.name: MIT
license.notes: Card tag license mit; no LICENSE file in the repo (404, 2026-11-19), text not read.

architecture.kind: sparse MoE with hybrid sliding-window attention, omni encoders
architecture.attention: 60 sliding-window layers (window 128) and 10 global-attention layers, 128 Q / 8 KV heads
architecture.why_this_design: The card lists the configuration but gives no reasons for the sliding-window to global ratio or the expert count.

variants.notes: MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL is the predecessor; no GGUF opened

pc-12gb.notes: 573 GB weights against about 60 GB RAM budget

pc-32gb.notes: even at 128 GB RAM, only a very low-bit quant of a 1T model could be stored

strengths: Tool-call repetition fix as a documented, measured failure mode (vendor blog)
weaknesses: Far too large for any consumer class
soft.behavior: Vendor describes tool-call repetition in the RL-stage Pro model and a response-level repetition reduction for this checkpoint across context lengths and harnesses (figure only).
soft.maturity: Established lab; the Flash sibling is recorded as mimo-v2.6-flash-mopd.

tona_fit.reason: 1.02T parameters at 573 GB is outside every hardware class. The technique (MOPD against tool-call repetition) is the useful part and is already covered by the Flash record.

sources.note: README head, config.json and file sizes via the HF API

open_questions: Benchmark table of the checkpoint (not captured; see the technical report and the card figures)
